title: GVE Maintained Python Source Layout

scope.subject: maintained Python source placement, naming, ownership, dependency direction, and API boundaries

allowed_responsibilities: installed command-line or module entry points
prohibited_responsibilities: single-feature implementation without broad package ownership
root_module_requirements: The module responsibility is broad enough to define a package boundary, installed entry point, broad orchestration boundary, or explicitly supported public API.
The module name describes durable product functionality rather than implementation chronology.
The module does not exist merely because no functional namespace had previously been established.

functional_namespace_policy.principle: Use shallow namespaces organized by stable functional ownership.
creation_criteria_any: an accepted near-term change requires multiple owned modules
prevents package-root accumulation or dependency cycles

naming_policy.required_style: stable functional snake_case for Python package, module, plugin, and action identifiers

ownerless_name_exception.requirement: A future exception requires separately accepted normative authority with narrow ownership and dependency rules.

rules: Each repository-owned plugin has exactly one owning directory.
Plugin-wide code remains at the plugin directory level.
Action-specific code remains in one action_<action_name>.py module.
One concrete plugin must not import another concrete plugin implementation directly.
Shared behavior belongs to a clearly owned framework or functional namespace.
Reserved paths do not require directory creation.
Reservation does not authorize discovery, loading, registration, execution, concrete plugins, concrete actions, or Stage 3 behavior.
External plugins may be separately distributed and are not required to live in this repository tree.

dependency_rules.statement: Installed product code must not import specification tooling, repository scripts, or tests.

principles: Importability alone does not create a supported compatibility promise.
Supported public package API, installed entry points, maintained internal modules, and test-only imports are distinct classifications.
Relocations preserve explicitly supported public interfaces or use separately accepted compatibility handling.

prohibited_paths.reason: chronology, issue, phase, milestone, temporary, or replacement-generation naming

current_tree_classification.notes: Only explicitly exported names are compatibility promises.
Non-entry-point contents remain internal unless explicitly supported.

current_tree_classification.functional_responsibility: broad product orchestration and maintained product behavior

current_tree_classification.successor_requirement: Relocation requires a separately governed dependent issue and must preserve exact behavior.

validation_requirements: Validate this document against its dedicated closed schema.
Confirm this document is outside specs/levels/.
Include this document exactly once in applicable normative discovery, identity, and revision mechanisms.
Do not validate this document as a level document.
Classify every maintained src/gve/**/*.py path exactly once.
Reject prohibited chronological and ownerless names.
Enforce plugin and action path patterns when those paths exist.
Permit reserved paths without requiring them to exist.
Reject installed product imports from specs, scripts, or tests.
Leave installed runtime behavior and entry points unchanged.
exclusions: relocation or semantic modification of src/gve/processing_failure.py
plugin discovery, loading, registration, or execution
installed entry-point or runtime behavior changes
